chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

A man from the Banu Fulan was mentioned to him, so he said: 'We only oppose them when we are with these people who rose up in Kufah.' He said: 'Fight them, for indeed the offspring of Fulan are like the Turks and the Romans, and they are a frontier (thighr) among the frontiers of the enemy, so fight them.'

key_terms.الثَّغْر: Thighr (a frontier or border region, often used for military contexts)
key_terms.بَنِي فُلاَنٍ: Banu Fulan (a specific tribe or family)
key_terms.بِالْكُوفَةِ: In Kufah (a major city in Iraq)

ai.seo_question: What is the reason for fighting the Banu Fulan according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) delineates the conditions for fighting a specific tribe, Banu Fulan, by linking their status to their alliance with the Kufah rebels. He characterizes them as a 'thighr' (frontier/fortress) of the enemy, comparable to the Turks and Romans, thereby justifying military engagement against them as a strategic necessity. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of evaluating tribal alliances and geographical strategic value in the context of civil conflict (Qital al-Ahl al-Bagh).
